Size the domain of the registered Axe finisher lever (hero_axe.lua X.ConsiderR, GH #115 section 5; no gate id written). The constant nKillDamage = 150 + 100*lv is 250/350/450 while Culling Blade's live damage is 275/375/475, so the bot declines a Culling that would kill whenever the target's effective health sits in the 25-point band [150+100*lv, damage[lv]). MEASURE IT ON THE EVENT SIDE, NOT THE FRAME SIDE -- this is the whole point of the request. Count Culling Blade CASTS, and separately the moments where Axe had Culling ready with an enemy hero inside 175u whose health was in the band and no cast followed. Record for each such moment: Culling rank, target health, target max health, distance, and whether the target died within the next 5s to anything.
requests.acceptance: An episode count in the shape the hero stream's other pre-flights use (N frames / M episodes / K games) PLUS at least one concrete (game, t) pair with a band-occupied target inside 175u, so a real-frame fixture can be cut with make_fixture.py. WHY THE FRAME CORPUS CANNOT ANSWER THIS (pre-registered, do not repeat the mistake): the repo's 100-frame fixture library gives 26 Axe frames, 20 Culling-ready, and only 3 with any enemy inside the branch's effective 375u ring -- against a 25-point band on a ~1000 health pool the expected hit count is ~0.08, so its zero is UNDERPOWERED and must NOT be reported as an empty domain. A frame-side scan of the archive has the same defect unless it yields hundreds of in-ring frames; the cast-side stream does not. TWO CORRECTIONS TO GH #115's PRE-REGISTERED TEXT: (1) it says 'target is inside 175', but the firing loop iterates J.GetAroundEnemyHeroList(nCastRange + 200), i.e. an EFFECTIVE 375u ring -- the bare cast-range list is computed and never read -- so report both rings; (2) count episodes, not frames.
